children: Palm oil strengthened, with the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for November delivery rising by 50 ringgit to 4,979 ringgit a ton. Prices were likely supported by persistent concerns about outlook over El Nino-related hot and dry weather conditions that could affect yields and future production, Kenanga Futures writes in a note. Investors remain watchful of August industry data from the Malaysian Palm Oil Board due later this week, it adds. (kimberley.kao@wsj.com)
